thread:
maria: Heads up — billing spike for a Redwood Dedicated customer in eu-west-1 this billing cycle. Charges jumped ~48% vs our committed estimate. Looking into commit sizing and whether the customer should bump their reserved capacity or we handle via burst credits. Any quick thoughts?
ajay: who is the customer? do we have the billing export?
maria: AcmeHealth-prod (acct-998). Billing export shows reserved capacity exhausted on 2026-02-03 and on-demand filled the rest. cost delta about $14k. Query I ran:
```
SELECT date, sku, usage_hours, cost
FROM billing_export
WHERE customer_account = 'acct-998' AND month = '2026-02'
ORDER BY date;
```
ajay: thanks. SRE bot shows ReservedPoolUsage hit 100% on 2026-02-03 04:12 UTC and stayed >95% for ~30m. :eyes:
sre-bot: Alert: ReservedPoolUsage >= commit_capacity (eu-west-1) at 2026-02-03T04:12Z. Fallback to OnDemand triggered.
kevin: quick context — the contract commit was sized for steady throughput ~4k tokens/s (approx equivalent to 2 A10s sustained for our model mix). Observed workload: baseline ~4k but p95 spikes to ~12k for short windows (1–3m). That mismatch is the root cause.
emma: finance: we saw $14,200 of on-demand overage this month for that account. They have a negotiated 20% discount band if they increase commit to cover spikes. Also they asked for clearer commit tiers (baseline vs burst).
julie (acct exec): client is open to short-term bump for a special quarter if we can present clear numbers. They dislike surprise on-demand bills.
ajay: capacity-wise in eu-west-1 right now we have ~8 available A10 equiv slots and 2 H100s unallocated. If we want to support a committed 12k tokens/s steady shape, rough estimate is 6 A10-equivalent GPUs (because of IO + batch smoothing) — which is 4 more than current commit. We can provision but lead time for dedicated physical attachments / network carve-outs is ~48–72h for private deployments.
kevin: proposal options we should surface to the customer:
- Option A: Increase monthly commit to cover 12k peak (steady commit). Pros: predictable billing. Cons: higher monthly cost.
- Option B: Keep baseline commit at 4k + burst credits pool (pay-as-you-burst but with capped monthly overage). Pros: cheaper baseline; Cons: still potential overage unless we offer guaranteed burst budget.
- Option C: Implement automated fallback policy + soft cap: if burst > 3x baseline, route to cheaper model variant (quantized) to reduce on-demand cost.
kevin: rough numbers (back-of-envelope): baseline 4k -> commit of 2 A10 equiv = $X/month (internal pricing table). Bump to 12k -> commit of 6 A10 equiv -> delta ~ +$28k/month. Burst credit cap (covering current spikes) -> one-time buffer purchase ~ $6k/month to avoid on-demand.
emma: to avoid surprises we can also propose a 90-day trial: temporarily increase commit to 12k, apply proration and then renegotiate based on observed 90-day utilization. Finance is ok if legal gives a short amendment.
ajay: one operational constraint: eu-west-1 GPU inventory is fragmented by tenant isolation. If we move them to a different region for capacity (e.g., eu-central-1) we need cross-region routing and additional egress costs. Client prefers eu-west-1 for latency/regulatory reasons.
maria: action items
1) ajay: do a concrete capacity runbook for eu-west-1 (exact free GPUs, expected lead times, which machine types) — ETA EOD UTC.
2) kevin: put together 3 commit proposals (A/B/C) with exact monthly cost deltas and expected unit throughput numbers. Include burst-credit pricing. ETA tomorrow morning.
3) julie + emma: draft amendment language for temporary 90-day commit bump and map financial impact to billing export to show client. ETA EOD.
4) infra ops: if commit is increased, plan for network carve-outs and autoscaling guards to avoid future runaway shards.
kevin: also recommend we add a new metric to the console: "reserved headroom %" (current reserved capacity vs p95 demand) so customers can self-detect sizing gaps.
maria: +1 that would help. Any objections to offering a one-time burst credit package while we negotiate commit?
emma: fine from finance. We'll cap it, and require signoff on amendment to avoid open-ended credits.
ajay: ok - will start capacity checks now. ping me if you want to join the infra debug call in 20.
maria: thanks all. tagging @sre-bot for a summary export when ajay posts the runbook. :thumbsup:
